answer: The BLIS configuration space for Qwen3-14B on H100 at rate=100 has a Pareto front with ~27 unique objective vectors (from 1800 total configs). The space is dominated by GPU allocation (tp × num_instances), which determines both throughput capacity and the GPU-cost objective. Within each GPU allocation, total_kv_blocks has a 'sufficiency threshold' below which preemptions degrade performance and above which adding more blocks has zero effect. This threshold depends on the (tp, num_instances, max_num_running_reqs) combination. block_size=32 always dominates or ties block_size=16 (larger blocks reduce fragmentation and preemptions). scheduler=fcfs Pareto-dominates sjf (SJF gets ~5% higher RPS but ~10% worse TTFT p99 in all tested cases). max_num_running_reqs matters primarily in single-instance configs near saturation: mrr=256 can eliminate soft saturation where mrr=128 cannot, despite zero preemptions in both cases. The key trade-off is throughput vs cost: higher TP gives better per-GPU throughput (tp=8 reaches 32 rps at 8 GPUs) while multiple instances give better latency (tp=4×2 gets 26.78 rps with 30ms TTFT p99 vs tp=8×1 getting 32 rps with 28ms at same 8 GPUs but needing 4000 vs 3000 KV blocks). The search algorithm uses a 5-phase approach: baseline scan, KVB sweep with soft-saturation detection (checking both preemption count AND RPS/TTFT degradation vs generous baseline), MRR sweep, scheduler/block-size verification, and gap-filling. It finds all 27+ Pareto-optimal objective vectors using 200 evaluations (11% of the space).
